content:
Requirement R11 (input): Input New UAV Parameters. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. Intent: Allow the pilot to set new operating parameters for a UAV..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-11.1, F-11.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: one distinct interaction idea per fixed modality pathway (e.g. one Touch-only, one Keyboard-only), plus a Mixed pathway if it adds real value beyond the two. Labeled Be-11.<F>.1, Be-11.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-11.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent restated:** R11 lets the pilot set new operating parameters (speed, altitude, heading) for a UAV under control, via Touch and Keyboard.

**Function candidates:**

**F-11.1 — Enable pilot authoring/entry of new UAV flight parameter values.**
Goal: provide the pilot the capability to specify target numeric values (SPD/ALT/HDG) for the UAV. Teleology is the *input/authoring* effect — the artefact exists to capture pilot-intended UAV setpoints. (Analogous to R01 for the ownship AP, but directed at the UAV.)

**F-11.2 — Ensure only valid/in-envelope UAV parameters are committed.**
Goal: prevent out-of-range or unsafe UAV setpoints from being dispatched. Teleology is the *safeguarding/gating* effect — the artefact exists to protect against erroneous commands reaching the UAV in a high-workload cockpit.

**F-11.3 — Confirm the pilot's parameter command was accepted by the UAV.**
Goal: close the loop so the pilot knows the UAV applied the new values (maps to steps 5.2.5–5.2.8 acknowledgment). Teleology is the *acknowledgment/awareness* effect.

**Note on scope/reuse:** F-11.2 (validation gate) and F-11.3 (ack confirmation) are strong reuse candidates — F-11.2 mirrors the R01/R05/R07 validation-gate pattern, and F-11.3 mirrors the R02/R05 multi-channel confirmation framework. The genuinely *new* goal for R11 is **F-11.1** (authoring UAV setpoints). The stated intent ("set new operating parameters") points squarely at F-11.1.

I recommend closing on **F-11.1** as the primary function for this requirement, treating validation and ack as reused behaviours to be referenced rather than re-designed here.

Which function do you want to close on?
Pretty much the same as R01, no?

Yes — functionally near-identical to R01. Both are "enable pilot authoring/entry of flight parameter values (SPD/ALT/HDG) via Touch+Keyboard, gated by envelope validation."

The **only** difference is the target: R01 sets ownship autopilot; R11 sets the UAV's setpoints. Same modalities, same value-entry goal, same validation pattern.

Two implications:

1. **Function** is essentially a re-parameterization of F-11.1 ≈ R01's function, scoped to the UAV rather than ownship. No genuinely distinct new goal here.

2. **The reuse flag is the real design decision:** the entry *mechanism* (multi-input keypad/OSS/rotary + validation gate) is a shared structure candidate. The question is whether the UAV param panel is the **same panel** as R01's (context-switched by target) or a **separate parallel panel**. That's a Structure-layer call — but worth flagging now because it drives whether R11 adds new structure at all.

So: close **F-11.1 — Enable pilot authoring/entry of new UAV flight parameter values**, explicitly noted as the UAV-scoped twin of R01's function. Agree?
Function should be the same, but the panels shouldn't be. The user should be able to do both at the same time, so two separate panels would be best.

Agreed. Function closed, panels separated.

**F-11.1 (closed) — Enable pilot authoring/entry of new UAV flight parameter values (SPD/ALT/HDG).** UAV-scoped twin of R01's function; same teleology, distinct target.

**Structure constraint carried forward:** a **dedicated UAV parameter panel**, distinct from R01's ownship AP panel, so both can be active/visible simultaneously (concurrent ownship + UAV setpoint authoring). The entry *logic/widgets* may still reuse R01's pattern, but the panel instance is separate — no context-switching on a shared panel.

Moving to **Behaviour** for F-11.1. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. One pathway per modality plus a mixed pathway.

**Be-11.1.1 — Touch-only.**
Pilot opens the UAV param panel on WAD; taps a field (SPD/ALT/HDG) to focus it; enters the value via an on-screen touch keypad; taps CONFIRM. Envelope validation gates CONFIRM (reused R01 pattern). All three fields settable by touch alone.

**Be-11.1.2 — Keyboard-only.**
Pilot selects the target field via bezel OSS (field-step) or UCP; enters/steps the value via UCP alphanumeric keyboard or bezel rotary; confirms via a dedicated CONFIRM OSS. No touch needed — full task completable on bezel/UCP alone. (TDC available as cursor variant if you want relative pointing to a field, but not required.)

**Be-11.1.3 — Mixed.**
Pilot touches a field to focus it (fast target acquisition), types the value on UCP keyboard (precise numeric entry under vibration), confirms via either touch or OSS. Adds real value: touch for spatial selection, keyboard for stable digit entry in a turbulent cockpit — plays to each modality's strength.

Note: validation gate (F-11.2) and UAV ack display (F-11.3) are reused behaviours triggered at CONFIRM and on 5.2.7 respectively — referenced, not redesigned here.

All three viable and satisfy modality-complete redundancy. Which do you want to close on?

All three behaviours retained.

**Be-11.1.1 (Touch-only) — closed**
**Be-11.1.2 (Keyboard-only) — closed**
**Be-11.1.3 (Mixed) — closed**

Together they satisfy modality-complete redundancy: full task achievable via Touch alone, Keyboard alone, or any mix.

Moving to **Structure**. Concrete HMI elements on the fixed hardware, honoring the separate-panel constraint (distinct from R01's ownship AP panel, concurrently displayable).

**S-11.1.1 — Dedicated UAV Parameter Panel (WAD overlay), touch-primary**
- New WAD overlay panel titled UAV PARAMS, visually distinct from R01's AP panel, positioned to co-exist (tiled or offset-stacked) so both are simultaneously visible.
- Three labeled fields: SPD / ALT / HDG, each tap-to-focus.
- On-screen touch keypad for numeric entry.
- CONFIRM button, gated by the reused envelope-validation logic.
- Serves Be-11.1.1 fully; serves Be-11.1.3 (focus by touch).

**S-11.1.2 — Bezel/UCP control set bound to the UAV panel**
- Bezel OSS row: field-select (step through SPD/ALT/HDG) + CONFIRM OSS.
- Bezel rotary: value stepping for focused field.
- UCP alphanumeric keyboard: direct numeric entry for focused field.
- Same panel from S-11.1.1 renders the focused field/value state so keyboard/bezel edits are visible.
- Serves Be-11.1.2 fully; serves Be-11.1.3 (value entry).

**S-11.1.3 — Shared state/validation + ack indicator on the panel**
- Single UAV-param state model backing both S-11.1.1 and S-11.1.2 (any modality reads/writes the same focused field + pending values) — this is what guarantees redundancy without locking modalities to sub-steps.
- Reused validation gate (F-11.2 / R01 pattern) evaluating all three fields before CONFIRM enables.
- Ack indicator on the panel driven by the reused R02/F-11.3 confirmation framework, showing 5.2.7 UAV acknowledgment (accepted/applied).

**Reuse flags:**
- S-11.1.3's validation gate and ack indicator reuse R01/R02 frameworks — referenced, not duplicated.
- S-11.1.1 and S-11.1.2 are **new instances** (separate panel per your constraint), but their internal widget patterns clone R01's proven layout.
- The UCP keyboard, bezel OSS/rotary, and audio ping are shared hardware also serving R01 — physically shared, contextually bound to whichever panel holds focus.

Note: S-11.1.1, S-11.1.2, S-11.1.3 aren't alternatives here — they're complementary layers (touch surface, bezel/UCP surface, shared backing state) that together deliver all three behaviours. If you'd prefer I frame them as competing alternatives instead, say so; otherwise recommend keeping all three as the composed structure.
Structure should be the same as R01, no?

Structurally the *pattern* is the same as R01 — but not the same *instances*, because you set the separate-panel constraint.

What's genuinely reused from R01 (same instance):
- Validation-gate logic (envelope check before CONFIRM)
- UCP keyboard, bezel OSS, bezel rotary — shared physical hardware
- Ack/confirmation framework (R02)

What's necessarily new (per your "two separate panels, both at once" call):
- The **UAV PARAMS panel instance** on WAD — distinct overlay from R01's AP panel, co-displayable
- The **binding** of the shared bezel/UCP hardware to *this* panel's focus state (context-bound, not a new control)
- The **UAV param state model** — separate from ownship AP state, so both can hold pending values concurrently

So: same widget layout, same interaction logic, same hardware — **cloned pattern**, but a **second parallel instance** with its own panel and state. If it were the *same* structure, you couldn't author ownship and UAV params simultaneously, which is exactly what you required.

Concretely, that collapses my three S-items into: **S-11.1.1 (new UAV panel instance, layout cloned from R01) + reused R01/R02 logic and hardware bound to it.**

Want to close on that — "R11 structure = R01 structure pattern, instantiated as a separate concurrent UAV panel with its own state"?
Yes, same structure pattern but instantiated as a separate panel with its own state.

**Structure closed.**

**S-11.1 (closed) — R01 structure pattern, re-instantiated as a separate, concurrently-displayable UAV PARAMS panel with its own state.**
- New WAD overlay panel instance (SPD/ALT/HDG fields, touch keypad, CONFIRM), layout cloned from R01's AP panel, co-displayable so ownship and UAV authoring run in parallel.
- Own UAV-param state model, distinct from ownship AP state.
- Reused (same instance): envelope-validation gate, R02 ack/confirmation framework, and shared bezel OSS/rotary + UCP keyboard hardware — context-bound to this panel's focus.

**R11 summary:**
- **F-11.1** — Enable pilot authoring/entry of new UAV flight parameter values (UAV-scoped twin of R01's function).
- **Be-11.1.1 / .2 / .3** — Touch-only, Keyboard-only, Mixed pathways; modality-complete redundancy.
- **S-11.1** — R01 pattern, separate panel instance with own state; validation, ack, and physical controls reused.

Ready for you to close R11, or move on.
